question: Just a few days apart, two people in Italy died of the A/H1N1 virus. H1N1, often mistakenly confused with swine flu, has been circulating every flu season since 2009. The main symptoms are a runny nose, sore throat, cough, fever, fatigue and breathing difficulties. In the most severe cases, these symptoms can turn lethal. A recent WHO report confirms that the mortality rate overlaps with the prepandemic level.

Hospital monitoring by general practitioners and paediatricians remains, in any case, important, as experts say that influenza causes 8 000–10 000 deaths per year, and 80 % of flu cases in Italy are currently caused by the H1N1 strain. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Commission concerned about the rapid spread of this virus?
What will it do to limit its spread?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.3.2024) Influenza A/H1N1 (officially called A(H1N1)pdm09 or A(H1)pdm09) is a seasonal influenza virus that has been commonly circulating since the 2009 influenza pandemic, and is not to be considered a novel influenza virus subtype.

The current assessment is that this influenza season, with relatively higher circulation of seasonal influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus, is not worse than expected. The current influenza season has been so far driven predominantly by A(H1)pdm09 (i.e. seasonal influenza A/H1N1 virus) in most EU countries, although also influenza A/H3N2 virus has been dominant or co-dominant in a smaller number of EU countries.

Severe disease due to influenza has mainly affected adults. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) continues to monitor the circulation and spread of influenza in the EU/European Economic Area (EEA) on a weekly basis through the European Respiratory Viruses Surveillance Summary (ERVISS)1.

The ECDC issued public health recommendations2 to the Member States on 15 December 2023 for reducing the impact of influenza and other respiratory viruses during the current winter season, which are still considered valid. This includes the use of vaccination against influenza in risk groups and of antivirals according to the national recommendations.

The ECDC is also monitoring the available estimates of effectiveness of vaccination against influenza and of resistance against antivirals during the current influenza season. The ECDC publishes seasonal influenza annual epidemiological reports for comparison with the recent past3.
